open_points.subject: Owner-session expiry pass
open_points.text: “a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start”
open_points.question: When is the first pass, and after a delayed pass is the next pass tied to the original 60-second schedule or to completion of the delayed pass?
options: Run immediately at process start and then on fixed 60-second boundaries
Run first 60 seconds after start and then on fixed boundaries
Wait 60 seconds after each completed pass
open_points.default_guess: Run first 60 seconds after start and then on fixed 60-second boundaries.

open_points.subject: Owner request versus expiry pass
open_points.text: “its arrival restarts the 30 minutes” and “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock and deciding under them”
open_points.question: How is an arriving request's validity check and last-request update ordered atomically against the expiry pass's decision, and does the request take the session lock for that operation?
options: The request takes the session lock and either refreshes the session before the pass or finds it ended
Arrival refreshes the timestamp without the session lock, with a separately defined atomic ordering
The pass may end a session concurrently with a request that has just refreshed it
open_points.default_guess: Take the session lock for the validity check and last-request update, giving the request or the pass one definite order.

open_points.subject: Admitted file request versus expiry cleanup
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs” and “the upload of a session ended by its limits goes with the session, when Registry ends it”
open_points.question: If an upload, mapping, confirmation or sign-out passes the session check but waits for the import/session locks, may the expiry pass end and remove that session before the admitted request acquires the locks, and if so how can that request still complete without recreating state in an ended session?
options: An admitted request prevents expiry cleanup until it finishes
Cleanup may end the session and the admitted request is then cancelled despite having passed the check
Cleanup may end the session, but the admitted request completes without retaining any session state
The request may recreate or retain state after the session was ended
open_points.default_guess: Count an admitted request as in flight and prevent expiry cleanup from removing its session until it finishes.

open_points.subject: Expiry-pass lock scope
open_points.text: “taking the import lock and then each session's lock”
open_points.question: Does one pass hold the import lock while it visits every session, or release and reacquire it for each session; and which sessions belong to the pass when sessions are created or signed out during iteration?
options: Hold the import lock for the whole pass and visit a snapshot of sessions taken under it
Reacquire the import lock per session and visit a snapshot
Reacquire per session and use a live collection
open_points.default_guess: Hold the import lock for the whole pass and visit a snapshot taken after acquiring it.

open_points.subject: Import-lock request admission
open_points.text: “take the instance's one import lock first, then their session's lock, check the closure while holding them, and hold both until done”
open_points.question: After an owner request has passed the session check but before it acquires the import lock, what event is its semantic ordering point against an accepted import or session expiry: session-check time, import-lock acquisition, session-lock acquisition, or transaction commit?
options: Import-lock acquisition determines its order
Session-lock acquisition determines its order
The initial session check determines its order
The database commit determines its order
open_points.default_guess: Import-lock acquisition determines its order against import closure, while the session lock determines its order against other changes to that session.

open_points.subject: Configuration well-formedness
open_points.question: What exact syntax and validity checks make the store location, backup location, owner credential, backup key and service tokens well formed beyond the separately stated length, distinctness and path checks?
options: Only successful decoding plus the explicitly listed checks
A declared character encoding and syntax for each item
Arbitrary environment strings or byte sequences are accepted for secrets, with paths parsed by the host platform
open_points.default_guess: Treat configuration as UTF-8 strings, require nonempty valid paths, and apply only the explicitly listed checks to secrets.

open_points.subject: Secret byte length and equality
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long” and “No two secrets are equal”
open_points.question: How are environment-variable text values converted to bytes for the 32-byte check, constant-time comparison and distinctness check, including non-ASCII text and any normalization?
options: UTF-8 encode exactly as supplied with no Unicode normalization
Restrict secrets to an ASCII encoding
Measure characters rather than encoded bytes
Decode a declared binary encoding such as base64 before checking
open_points.default_guess: Require ASCII secrets and compare their exact encoded bytes.

open_points.subject: Configuration check precedence in owner-only mode
open_points.text: “one service token for each service ... or, for an owner-only start, none of the four” and “every item of rule 1 present”
open_points.question: At what point is all-four versus owner-only mode selected, and which deterministic failure is reported when only some service-token variables are present or one is malformed?
options: Select owner-only only when all four variables are absent; otherwise require and validate all four in table order
Validate every present token first, then decide whether the set is complete
Treat any incomplete token set as an unknown configuration mode
open_points.default_guess: Select owner-only only when all four are absent; otherwise require and validate all four in A09 table order.

open_points.subject: Store integrity check
open_points.question: What exact integrity procedure and pass criteria are required at startup and during backup checking?
options: Use only the database engine's built-in full integrity check
Check engine integrity plus Registry schema, constraints and referential invariants
Use a release-specific Registry integrity procedure declared elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Run the database engine's full integrity check and validate the release's schema and foreign-key constraints.

open_points.subject: Concurrent Registry starts
open_points.text: “Registry makes a new, empty store ... under a temporary name ... that it renames to the store's name only once the store is complete”
open_points.question: What happens if two Registry processes start concurrently against the same store and backup locations, including competing probe files, temporary-store cleanup and final rename?
options: An instance-level lock permits only one process to start
Atomic create/rename makes one process win and the other fail without deleting the winner's temporary files
Concurrent processes are an excluded deployment error
open_points.default_guess: Acquire an exclusive instance lock covering startup, serving and backup work.

open_points.subject: Startup probe cleanup
open_points.text: “A failed start leaves no file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run removes with the other temporary files”
open_points.question: What exact name identifies a probe, when does the next start remove it, and does failure to remove an old probe stop startup or merely produce a diagnostic?
options: Probe files use the backup temporary prefix and inability to remove any of them stops startup
A unique probe name is removed opportunistically and failure is only reported
The next backup run, not startup, owns cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Use the backup temporary prefix; remove all such files before probing, and stop startup if any cannot be removed.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, key derivation or key interpretation, nonce generation, versioning and associated-data rules must implementations use?
options: A specified AEAD format with a fresh random nonce and authenticated metadata
Backend-selected authenticated encryption
Encryption without authenticated integrity, relying on the later store check
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD format with a fresh random nonce and authenticate all cleartext metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: Backup cleartext metadata
open_points.text: “It records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key”
open_points.question: Is the cleartext record authenticated by the encrypted backup, what digest algorithm and encoding identify the key, and what validation prevents parseable but false metadata such as a future instant or wrong sequence number from counting as valid?
options: Authenticate canonical metadata as AEAD associated data and validate all fields against the decrypted store
Leave metadata unauthenticated and validate only that its fields parse
Put a signed or keyed authentication tag on the metadata separately
open_points.default_guess: Encode metadata canonically, authenticate it as AEAD associated data, and compare its release and sequence facts with the decrypted store while rejecting impossible instants.

open_points.subject: Empty or pruned audit log in a backup
open_points.text: “checks ... that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: How is the recorded last sequence number defined and checked when the store has never written an audit entry, or when old entries were erased and the durable next-sequence counter is greater than the highest remaining entry?
options: Record and verify the durable last-issued counter, using 0 before the first entry
Record the greatest sequence number still present, using 0 when none remains
Record both the last-issued counter and greatest retained entry
open_points.default_guess: Record and verify the durable last-issued sequence counter, with 0 before any entry, independently of which entries remain.

open_points.subject: Backup file format and kept name
open_points.text: “A kept name is made from the backup's instant and is never overwritten”
open_points.question: What canonical timestamp precision, filename encoding and collision rule are used when two backups have the same recorded instant or when different textual instants map to the same filesystem name?
options: Use a fixed UTC format with sufficient precision plus a unique random suffix
Use the instant alone and fail on any collision as stated
Use the instant plus the audit sequence number
open_points.default_guess: Use a canonical UTC timestamp plus the snapshot's last sequence number, and fail rather than overwrite if that name exists.

open_points.subject: Backup retention bound
open_points.text: “at most 31 days after the erasure” and “Registry bounds neither how long a run takes”
open_points.question: Is 31 days a hard bound, or can an overlapping, delayed or arbitrarily long run extend retention even when runs do not otherwise fail?
options: 31 days is a hard bound, requiring a bound on run duration and scheduling delay
31 days applies only when a successful deletion step completes daily; any missed, overlapping or long run extends it
There is no maximum retention bound
open_points.default_guess: Treat 31 days as conditional on a successful deletion step completing each day; every missed, overlapping, failed or long-running backup extends retention.

open_points.subject: Backup check coverage
open_points.text: “opens that for reading only, checks that it is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: Does a checked backup also have to prove that every required Registry record, schema constraint and cross-record invariant is readable and valid, including the deliberate absence of agent sessions, or are engine integrity, version and sequence checks sufficient?
options: Validate the full release schema and all durable domain invariants
Validate only engine integrity, store version and audit sequence
Validate engine and schema constraints but not higher-level domain invariants
open_points.default_guess: Validate engine integrity, the exact release schema, foreign-key and uniqueness constraints, absence of agent sessions, and the recorded audit counter.

open_points.subject: Backup-key rotation and restorability
open_points.text: “older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with” and “decrypting an older one, with the key it was made with, is part of a restore, outside Registry”
open_points.question: What requirement ensures that the owner retains and can identify every old backup key for as long as a backup encrypted with it is kept, and what should happen to an old backup whose key is unavailable?
options: The owner must retain old keys outside Registry until their backups expire
Registry retains old keys in protected configuration state
Backups whose key is unavailable remain kept but are not guaranteed restorable
Backups whose key is unavailable are deleted
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain old keys outside Registry until every backup made with them has expired; Registry keeps such backups unchanged.
